## Repeat the nearest owned cell (`extrapolation`) {#sec-ch11-extrapolation}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0
status: draft
-->

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Fill every ghost layer with the same boundary-adjacent owned cell. This is the zero-gradient copy condition.
Default: off; fallback for outflow auxiliary scalars and shallow water.
Order: exact discrete operation or local derivation below; coupled solver order not measured.
:::

### Derivation

For a smooth field with a prescribed zero normal derivative, a constant extension supplies ghost values.
The discrete rule is the nearest owned-cell average repeated at every ghost depth:

$$
q_{i-l}=q_i.
$$ {#eq-ch11-extrapolation-copy}

At the lower wall $i$ is the first owned index and $l=1,\ldots,n_g$; the upper rule uses the last owned cell.
`extrapolation_inner` ([`bc_func.cpp:52-66`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L52-L66)) broadcasts a width-one slab, implementing @eq-ch11-extrapolation-copy.
For a general smooth field, Taylor expansion between the donor and ghost centroids gives a leading difference
proportional to their separation times the normal derivative, hence $O(h)$ at fixed depth on a uniform grid.
This is a consistency estimate for ghost values, not a measured solver convergence rate. C1 checks exact
constant preservation and idempotence.

The report-only checks are `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`; their current output is
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`. They do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

Collapsed axes are skipped. Primitive, conserved and scalar calls all use the same copy. `radiating`
selects this fallback before validating EOS and reference context for auxiliary `kScalar` fields or shallow water.
Thus an auxiliary limiter field does not undergo the acoustic split. This callback runs with physical fills,
including the supported corner refresh.

: Implementation sites for extrapolation. {#tbl-ch11-extrapolation-code}

1. Select the first or last owned width-one slab. The anchor `extrapolation_inner` is in [`bc_func.cpp:52-66`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L52-L66).
2. Broadcast it to the whole ghost slab without changing owned cells. The anchor `extrapolation_inner` is in [`bc_func.cpp:52-66`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L52-L66).
3. Use the same operation for the early scalar/shallow-water outflow fallback. The anchor `radiating` is in [`bc_func.cpp:108-133`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/bc_func.cpp#L108-L133).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Zero gradient is not an acoustic nonreflection condition. The pulse test prints an extrapolation
comparison but only asserts the outflow arm, so no measured reflection fraction for extrapolation is claimed.

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result is claimed.
:::
